summary:
[  edit  ]
The Beat  CHOP  generates a variety of ramps, pulses and counters that are timed to the beats per minute and the sync as produced by the  Beat Dialog .
You can generate a ramp every 1/4 1/2 1 2 4 8 32 beats.
You can generate ramps of any other length, like 12 beats per bar (ramp) and fractional beats like 3.33 beats per ramp.
You can generate a set of channels, where each channel is delayed relative to the prior channel. This is useful, for example, for moving eight objects delayed by one beat each.
There also is a counter of how many ramps it has generated.
The Count+Ramp type generates a continuously-rising ramp equal to the number of cycles since the start.
If Play Mode is set to Local Sequential, it doesn't look at start/end of the timeline (i.e. doesn't reset when the timeline loops), so is more appropriate for long improvised playing.
Note:  for the purposes of this dialog, a  bar  is 4 beats and the  period  is the number of beats set by the Period parameter.
The  Beat Dialog  is used to manually tap the beat to set the beats-per-minute (BPM). The Beat  CHOP  converts the BPM into a repeating ramp or pulse that keeps time with the music after you stop tapping.
You can set the global beats-per-minute with the python command:   op('/local/time').tempo = 140
The phase can be controlled with the Beat  CHOP 's Reset parameters.
The Beat  CHOP 's timing is defined by the  Component Time  of the  Reference   Node .  If the  Reference  Node parameter is left blank, then the time defined at the Beat  CHOP 's location is used. The default is in  /local/time .
See also:  Timeline CHOP ,  Time COMP .

parameters.label: Reference   Operator
parameters.name: op
parameters.description: This node is used to specify the time settings referenced by the Beat  CHOP . The time is defined by the Time  COMP  found at  timepath(" reference_node ")

parameters.label: Use  Reference   Time Slice
parameters.name: reftimeslice
parameters.description: Turn on this checkbox to use the  Time Slicing  used by the  Reference   Node .

parameters.label: Play Mode
parameters.name: playmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the method used to playback the output.

parameters.label: Locked to  Timeline
parameters.name: locked
parameters.description: This mode locks the output to the local component  Timeline . Scrubbing or jumping in the local time will update the output accordingly. When the local timeline loops the output is reset and starts over. The output will be the same for each pass through the local timeline.

parameters.label: Locked to Global
parameters.name: global
parameters.description: This mode locks the output to the Global beat source. It will follow the Beat  CHOP  with whose 'Update Global' flag is turned on.

parameters.label: Local Sequential
parameters.name: local
parameters.description: This mode produces a continuous output regardless of the timeline position.

parameters.label: Period
parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Number of beats it takes to generate one cycle of ramp.	Use the drop down menu to select from some commonly used Period lengths.

parameters.label: Multiples
parameters.name: multiples
parameters.description: The number of channels to create.

parameters.label: Shift Offset
parameters.name: shiftoffset
parameters.description: Delays all channels by this amount. 0 = no change, .5 means 50% of one period later.

parameters.label: Shift Step
parameters.name: shiftstep
parameters.description: When set to 1, and Multiples is 5, each ramp channel is 1/5 cycle later than the previous channel. When set to .1, the delay is 1/50 cycle. This is a way to stagger the channels.

parameters.label: Random Offset
parameters.name: randoffset
parameters.description: The amount that each ramp is randomly time-shifted relative to a perfect ramp.

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.name: randseed
parameters.description: Changing this generates a different set of random offsets.

parameters.label: Reset Condition
parameters.name: resetcondition
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu determines how the Reset input triggers a reset of the channel(s).

parameters.label: Off to On
parameters.name: offtoon
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes off to on.

parameters.label: While On
parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes on. The channel will hold the reset value until the input turns off.

parameters.label: On to Off
parameters.name: ontooff
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes on to off.

parameters.label: While Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes off. The channel will hold the reset value until the input turns on.

parameters.label: Reset Bar Value
parameters.name: resetbarvalue
parameters.description: Specifies which Bar the Beat  CHOP  will jump to when the Reset Condition is met. Beat values are derived from the fractional part of this value.

parameters.label: Wait after Reset
parameters.name: resetwait
parameters.description: When using the  While On  Reset Condition, Wait After Reset will hold the channels at zero until the next bar is started, after which the output will continue. When Wait After Reset is off, the channels will restart output as soon as the reset condition is done.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: This button resets the ramps to zero when On. The ramp is also zero when the Beat  CHOP 's input is above 0.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Instantly resets the ramps to zero.

parameters.label: Update Global
parameters.name: updateglobal
parameters.description: Any Beat  CHOP  can be made the "global beat source" by turning on Update Global. A reference Beat  CHOP  is created at /local/master_beat (if it doesn't already exist) and all Beat CHOPs can synchronize to this by setting 'Play Mode: Locked to Global'. That master Beat  CHOP  also needs 'Update Global' turned on, if not already on. This means you require exactly one master Beat  CHOP  per toe. You can turn switch back to 'Play Mode: Locked to Sequential' when desired.  $MASTER_BEAT is set to whatever Beat  CHOP  has this option turned on.

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.name: ramp
parameters.description: Outputs a 0-1 ramp each period.

parameters.label: Pulse
parameters.name: pulse
parameters.description: Outputs a pulse each period.

parameters.label: Sine
parameters.name: sine
parameters.description: Outputs a sine wave each period.

parameters.label: Count
parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Increases the count each period.

parameters.label: Count+Ramp
parameters.name: countramp
parameters.description: A ramp that counts up until the bar is reset.

parameters.label: Bar
parameters.name: bar
parameters.description: Output the current bar.

parameters.label: Beat
parameters.name: beat
parameters.description: Output the current beat.

parameters.label: Sixteenths
parameters.name: sixteenths
parameters.description: Output the current sixteenths.

parameters.label: Ramp Bar
parameters.name: rampbar
parameters.description: Outputs a 0-1 ramp each bar.

parameters.label: Ramp Beat
parameters.name: rampbeat
parameters.description: Outputs a 0-1 ramp each beat.

parameters.label: BPM
parameters.name: bpm
parameters.description: Outputs the current BPM.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
